successors.note: Italian Libya page: Tripolitania and Cyrenaica were under 'British military administration'; Italian East Africa page: all former Italian East African territories then came under British military administration. Request R140 (3 Nov 2026): the land lacked Eritrea and Italian Somaliland, which the text above names; without them the dissolve of 1943 handed those cells to nobody. British Military Administration (Eritrea) page: "British forces defeated the Italian army in Eritrea in 1941 at the Battle of Keren", the administration "was established following the Allied victory over Italy at the Battle of Keren in 1941" and continued "until 1950"; Italian Somaliland page: "British forces occupied Italian Somaliland and militarily administered the territory" and it "came under British military administration until 1950, when it became a United Nations trusteeship". The window patch p1940-p1949 gains both from italian-africa in February 1943 (events/4, 5); the cells are then already British at the dissolve, so the two do not clash.

keyframe_review.note: Italo-Turkish War page: by the end of 1912 Italian forces were 'in effect besieged in seven enclaves on the coasts of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica', the largest, at Tripoli, 'extended barely 15 kilometers (9.3 miles) from the town', and Italian ground forces 'were limited to a thin coastal strip'; the page says the Senussi order controlled most of Libya after the Treaty of Ouchy. Pacification of Libya page: Italy 'seized military control of coastal Libya, but large swaths of the interior remained under local Libyan rule'. Cliopatria's 2,946 Libyan cells in 1912 (Tripolitania 857 of its 928, northern Cyrenaica 704 of 2,496, western Fezzan 1,385 of 2,015, about 0.88 M km2) are the legal claim of the decree of 5 November 1911 and the treaty, not land held. Corrected: Libya is cut to the five enclaves of the towns the page names (the page names no other two of the seven); the interior is carried as contested land in the ledger (Senussi 1912-1917, Tripolitanian rebels 1918-1924 and later, Cyrenaica 1923-1932). The Somali part is as in 1900. 1912-1919: in 1914 the Fezzan was briefly Italian (August to November, ledger) and in 1915 the Italian Tripolitania page has the forces 'held only within coastal cities', retiring 'to Tripoli, Zuwara, and Al Khums'; no shape change is drawn for these months.

2.12 M km2 for 1932-1935. Libya now spans the coast, the Fezzan, Jarabub and Kufra; the Cyrenaican resistance ended in January 1932 ('in January 1932, Badoglio proclaimed the end of the campaign'). The Italian Libya page gives 1,759,541 km2 for 1939 (the whole of Libya) against about 1.29 M km2 of Libyan cells here; the Libyan shape is the smaller because the south-east (the Sarra triangle, 1934) is added by the ledger and the Tibesti and the Aouzou strip are not in the shape. The unification of the colonies as Italian Libya on 1 January 1934 changes no outline.

3.33 M km2 for 1936-1939, East Africa about 1.97 M km2 against the Italian East Africa infobox 1,725,000 km2 for 1939 (ratio 1.14, accepted). Ethiopia annexed 9 May 1936 and Italian East Africa proclaimed 1 June 1936. The Libyan part gains 283 cells over 1935 in the south-east, read as the Sarra Triangle (turned over to Italy in 1934; the ledger dates it); the Aouzou strip of the 1935 Mussolini-Laval agreement (which France never ratified) is not in the shape and not drawn. The incorporation of the coastal provinces into metropolitan Italy (9 January 1939) changes no outline because a colony is already drawn as a tint of the metropole.

3.51 M km2: the 1939 shape plus British Somaliland (877 cells, about 222,000 km2) occupied in August 1940; the page's infobox dates the annexation to 19 August 1940. The Italian Empire infobox gives 3,798,000 km2 for 1938 and 3,824,879 km2 for 1941 (the page does not say whether metropolitan Italy is counted); the African shape of 3.51 M km2 is within a factor of two of both.

correction.text: Shape unchanged; Cyrenaica drawn as contested with British forces (contest zone 1940-1942), the East African losses dated by the ledger

keyframe_review.note: Year-end shape: Libya plus the Gondar pocket (9 Ethiopian cells, 'the Battle of Gondar in November 1941', 27 November). Somalia, Eritrea, Addis Ababa and British Somaliland were lost earlier in 1941; the ledger gives the months, so the whole of East Africa is held from January until each loss. Libya: Operation Compass (Bardia 14 December 1940 to 5 January 1941, Tobruk 21 January, Beda Fomm 5-7 February) took Cyrenaica for the British until the Axis counter-offensive of March-April 1941 retook it ('Benghazi was captured in April'); Tobruk stayed besieged until the relief of November-December 1941. The ledger carries these swings and a contest zone over Cyrenaica; the year-end shape keeps Libya whole. The Italian posts at Kassala (left 18 January 1941) and Moyale are small ledger occupations.

region.text: Kassala and its district

ledger.note: 17 July 1894: Italy annexes Kassala to Italian Eritrea. 'On July 17, 1894, Italy annexed Kassala to Italian Eritrea.' The Mahdist State dossier has the matching loss; Cliopatria's 1895 shape of the Mahdist State still holds the town. The land is a town and its district, a small gain.

region.text: the Tigray front, Adigrat, Adwa, Mekelle

ledger.note: 1895: Italian troops march into Tigray. 'Baratieri promptly marched into Adigrat on March 8'; Adwa occupied 2 April (the page gives no year, the war began 13 January 1895).

region.text: Tigray province, annexed into Italian Eritrea

ledger.note: April 1895: Baratieri occupies Adigrat and Adwa and annexes Tigray. 'Promptly marched into Adigrat on March 8', 'occupied Adwa on April 2' (1895 from context) and issued a proclamation 'annexing Tigray province into Italian Eritrea' (no date for the proclamation). Italy also held Mekelle, where the Ethiopian forces surrounded the fort on 18 December 1895. Cliopatria draws no Tigray (23 Ethiopian cells); ethiopian-empire (af-01) should mirror the loss.

region.text: Kassala and its district

ledger.note: 1896 or later: Italy leaves Kassala. Kassala page: Italy's defeat at Adwa in 1896 'forced the Italians to evacuate the town', after which Anglo-Egyptian forces re-occupied it. The page gives no date for the evacuation itself, so 1896 is a bridge (confidence 1); the Mahdist State dossier has Kassala outside Mahdist hands by 1899. anglo-egyptian-sudan has no dossier yet.

region.text: Tigray: Mekelle, Adigrat and Adwa

ledger.note: 1896: Italy loses Tigray. The fort at Mekelle surrendered on 21 January 1896, Baratieri left Adigrat to move toward Adwa (no day on the page) and the Italians were beaten at Adwa on 1 March 1896; the month 3 is the battle, the withdrawal from the whole province is the researcher's reading. ethiopian-empire (af-01) should mirror the gain.

region.text: the Tigray front, Adigrat, Adwa, Mekelle

ledger.note: 1896: Menelik wins at Adwa and Italy recognises Ethiopia. 'The decisive battle of the war was the Battle of Adwa on March 1, 1896'; the October treaty 'delineated the borders of Eritrea' and forced Italy to recognise 'absolutely and without any reserve' the independence of Ethiopia (war ends 23 October 1896).
1897: Asmara becomes the capital of Eritrea. 'In 1897, Martini declared Asmara the capital of the colony.'

region.text: the coasts of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica

ledger.note: 1911: Italy declares war on the Ottoman Empire and lands in Libya. Italy declared war on the Ottoman Empire on 29 September 1911; Tripoli, Tobruk, Derna, Benghazi and Homs were taken 3-21 October; a decree of 5 November 1911 declared Italian sovereignty over Libya.

region.text: the coasts of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica

ledger.note: 1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war on 18 October. The Ottomans agreed to withdraw military personnel from the Tripoli and Benghazi vilayets, and the treaty 'gave Italy the possession of Libya'.

region.text: the coastal enclaves of Tripoli, Homs, Benghazi, Derna and Tobruk, the five towns the Italo-Turkish War page names; 20 km radius, the smallest circle the 16 km grid draws (the page gives about 15 km for Tripoli)

ledger.note: 18 October 1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war. The Ottomans 'would withdraw all military personnel from Trablus and Benghazi vilayets (Libya)' and Italy kept what it held: the page has Italy taking Tripoli, Tobruk, Derna, Bengasi and Homs between 3 and 21 October 1911 (Tobruk also 4 December) and, 'by the end of 1912', 'in effect besieged in seven enclaves on the coasts of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica', the largest at Tripoli reaching 'barely 15 kilometers' from the town. Only the five named towns are drawn; the interior (the Senussi order controlled most of it) is not gained, see the contest from October 1912. Cliopatria's 0.88 M km2 of Libyan interior is not a gain.

region.text: the interior of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica beyond the coastal enclaves

ledger.note: October 1912: the interior stays out of Italian hands. The page says the Senussi order, which refused to surrender, controlled most of Libya after the treaty; Italy claimed the whole in law (decree of 5 November 1911, Treaty of Ouchy). The page gives no date for the first clash, so October 1912 is the treaty month; counterpart senussi-order has no dossier yet.

region.text: the Fezzan, briefly under Italian suzerainty

ledger.note: August 1914: the Italian advance to Ghat puts the Fezzan briefly under Italian suzerainty. 'Italian advance to Ghat(August) makes Tripolitania (including Fezzan) initially under Italian suzerainty'. No holder is named, hence nobody.

region.text: the Fezzan, recaptured by the Libyan resistance

ledger.note: November 1914: the Fezzan is lost. 'because of the recapture of Sabha(November) by Libyan resistance men, the advance turns into retreat.' region.text: the interior of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica beyond the coastal enclaves

ledger.note: 1917: the Treaty of Acroma. The Pacification page: fighting with British forces lasted until 1917 and the treaty ended Senussi attacks on the British and Italians; the interior stays outside Italian control until the reconquest.

region.text: Tripolitania beyond the coastal enclaves, held by the rebels

Italy claims the interior in law and holds only the coast; counterpart tripolitanian-republic has no dossier yet.

ledger.note: 1922: Italian forces occupy Misrata. '1922: Italian forces occupy Misrata, launching the reconquest of Tripolitania.' The page gives the year only; the circle is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 26 January 1923: the Cyrenaica war begins. The Pacification page dates the war 26 January 1923 to 24 January 1932 (infobox) and has the Cyrenaica war fought mainly in the Jebel Akhdar; the Tripolitanian reconquest of 1923-1924 is the contest with the rebels (ledger 1918 and 1924).

region.text: Tripolitania beyond the coastal enclaves, held by the rebels

'From 1923 to 1924, Italian troops regained all territory north of the Ghadames-Mizda-Beni Ulid region'; the Italian Tripolitania page: '1924: With the conquest of Sirt, most of Tripolitania (except the Sirt desert) is in Italian hands.' The polygon through the three towns is the researcher's reading; dated to 1924, the year the reconquest of the north is complete.

region.text: Tripolitania south of the Ghadames-Mizda-Beni Ulid line (Ghibla)

ledger.note: 1924: the southern half of the rebel contest begins. What is left of Tripolitania after the northern line is retaken (Ghibla and the south) stays with the rebels until late 1928.

region.text: the Sirtica, about 150,000 km2 taken in five months (the two districts are the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1924: the Sirtica campaign. Italians 'occupied 150,000 square kilometres (58,000 sq mi) of territory in five months'. The page names no holder, hence nobody; the two districts are the researcher's reading.

region.text: Jubaland (Oltre Giuba), approximated by the three Somali regions on and beyond the Juba river

ledger.note: 1925: Britain cedes Jubaland (Oltre Giuba) and Italy merges it into Italian Somaliland. 'The transfer occurred in 1925'; the Italian Empire page: 'resolve the question of Jubaland in 1924, which was merged into Italian Somaliland'. Month not on the pages.

region.text: the Hobyo protectorate (central Somalia)

ledger.note: 1 October 1925: the protectorate of Hobyo ends. 'Three columns of dubats, under the command of Colonel Di Bello, entered the sultanate's territory' and occupied it 'completely within a few weeks and deposing the ruler' (Campaign of the Sultanates page); the Hobyo dossier dates the loss to October 1925. The Italian Somaliland page counts the annexation of both sultanates 'by the end of 1927'; Omar Samatar's revolt took Ceel Buur on 9 November 1925 and the Italians retook it on 26 December 1925.

region.text: the Hobyo protectorate (central Somalia)

ledger.note: 1 October 1925: Italy occupies Hobyo and deposes the sultan (Campaign of the Sultanates page: the columns entered on 1 October and the occupation was complete 'within a few weeks'). The first run dated the gain to 1927, the annexation of both sultanates ('By the end of 1927'); the Hobyo dossier has the occupation in October 1925, and this date now agrees with it.

region.text: the Majeerteen protectorate (northeast Somalia)

ledger.note: October 1925: the Majeerteen protectorate turns into war. The Campaign of the Sultanates page has the treaties abrogated before annexation (no date) and fighting at Alula and Hafun after the Italian landings; the protectorate ends with the contest below. 'By the end of 1927, the territories of Hobyo Sultanate and Majeerteen Sultanate' were annexed (Italian Somaliland page).

region.text: the Majeerteen sultanate (Bari, Nugaal)

ledger.note: October 1925: the Italians land at Alula and Hafun and fight the Majeerteen. The Governor ordered the sultan to surrender on 7 October 1925 and Baargaal was bombarded in November; the page gives no day for the landings. Matches the Majeerteen dossier (contest 1925-10 to 1927).

region.text: the Jarabub (Giarabub) district; Kufra followed in 1931

ledger.note: 1925: Egypt cedes the Jarabub oasis (and, on paper, the Kufra district) to Italian Libya. 'Egypt ceded Kufra and Jarabub districts to Italian Libya on December 6, 1925.' Kufra itself was taken in 1931.

region.text: the Majeerteen sultanate (Bari, Nugaal)

ledger.note: Late 1927: the Majeerteen are beaten. the Italians could not fully capture Majeerteenia 'until late 1927', after the fighting at Iskushuban sent Hersi Boqor and his staff into the Ogaden (the infobox puts the final stage in February-March 1927).

region.text: the Majeerteen protectorate (northeast Somalia)

ledger.note: End of 1927: Italy annexes the Majeerteen sultanate after the Campaign of the Sultanates (1925-1927). The Majeerteen 'eventually directly annexed to the Italian colony of Somalia' (Campaign of the Sultanates page); the Italian Somaliland page: 'By the end of 1927'.

region.text: Tripolitania south of the Ghadames-Mizda-Beni Ulid line (Ghibla)

ledger.note: Late 1928: the southern half of the rebel contest ends. 'By late 1928, the Italians had taken control of Ghibla, and its tribes were disarmed.'

region.text: Ghibla and the rest of Tripolitania south of the line

ledger.note: Late 1928: Italy takes Ghibla. 'By late 1928, the Italians had taken control of Ghibla, and its tribes were disarmed.' Ghibla is read as Tripolitania south of the Ghadames-Mizda-Beni Ulid line (the researcher's reading).

region.text: the Fezzan, to Tummo

ledger.note: 1930: Italian forces conquer the Fezzan. 'In 1930, Italian forces conquered Fezzan and raised the Italian flag in Tummo, the southernmost region of Fezzan.'

region.text: the Kufra district

ledger.note: 1931: Graziani seizes Kufra. 'In 1931, Italian forces seized Kufra where Senussi refugees were bombed and strafed by Italian aircraft as they fled into the desert.' (Italian Libya page: 'General Rodolfo Graziani easily conquered Kufra District'.)

region.text: Cyrenaica, mainly the Jebel Akhdar

ledger.note: 1932: the Cyrenaican resistance is crushed. 'Mukhtar's death effectively ended the resistance, and in January 1932, Badoglio proclaimed the end of the campaign.'

region.text: Cyrenaica beyond the coastal towns

ledger.note: January 1932: Cyrenaica beyond the coastal towns passes under Italian control. 'in January 1932, Badoglio proclaimed the end of the campaign'; the page says the campaign ended, not that every district was held.

region.text: the Sarra Triangle and the south-eastern corner of Libya (Cliopatria's 1936 addition of 283 cells, read as the Sarra Triangle)

ledger.note: 1934: the Sarra Triangle is turned over to Italy. 'Ma'tan as-Sarra was turned over to Italy in 1934 as part of the Sarra Triangle'; the page does not name the ceding party (read here as the Sudan side, inside Cliopatria's British Africa). The Aouzou strip, given to Italy by the Mussolini-Laval agreement of 1935 but never ratified by France, is not drawn: Cliopatria's shape leaves it out and the claim was never in force.

region.text: Ethiopia, annexed 9 May 1936

ledger.note: 1936: Italy takes Addis Ababa on 5 May and Mussolini annexes Ethiopia on 9 May. 'On 5 May 1936 the capital Addis Ababa was captured by the Italians'; infobox 'Ethiopia formally annexed: 9 May 1936'. Italian East Africa (Eritrea, Somalia, Ethiopia in six governorates) was proclaimed on 1 June 1936.

1939: the coastal provinces of Libya are incorporated into Italy. On 9 January 1939 'the coastal regions of the colony were incorporated into metropolitan Italy' (the Fourth Shore). A change of status within the Italian tint, so no outline changes.

region.text: Kassala

ledger.note: July 1940: the Italian offensive on the Sudanese border begins. 'on July 4, 1940 the Italians started their offensive with 2,500 men' (Kassala page); the East African campaign page: 'On 4 July 1940, the Italians launched a limited offensive to capture Sudanese settlements near the border'. Neither page gives the day Kassala fell.

region.text: Moyale

ledger.note: July 1940: Moyale. 'On 1 July, Moyale... was attacked' and the Italians attacked again 'on 10 July', after which 'the British withdrew unopposed'. The page gives no day for the Italian entry.

region.text: British Somaliland, the northern Somali coast

ledger.note: 1940: Italy annexes British Somaliland. 'In August 1940, the protectorate of British Somaliland was occupied by Italian forces'; infobox 'annexation' 19 August 1940.

region.text: the Egyptian coast from Sollum to Sidi Barrani and Sofafi

ledger.note: 13-18 September 1940: the Italian invasion of Egypt. 'The Italian invasion of Egypt on 13-18 September began as a limited tactical operation towards Marsa Matruh'; the Italians 'dug in around Sidi Barrani and Sofafi'. The strip from Sollum to Sidi Barrani is drawn as a 110 km circle at Salum cut to Egypt (Sidi Barrani is not in the gazetteer).

region.text: the Egyptian coast from Sollum to Sidi Barrani and Sofafi

ledger.note: 11 December 1940: 'the Italians were defeated at Sidi Barrani', the first battle of Operation Compass; the page does not date the last Italian post on Egyptian soil.

region.text: Cyrenaica, where the front swung from December 1940 to November 1942

ledger.note: December 1940: Operation Compass. 'Bardia fell between 14 December and 5 January 1941'; the first British ground in Libya. Cyrenaica is contested through the swings of 1941-1942.

region.text: Moyale

ledger.note: 1941: Moyale returns to the British. Neither page opened dates the British return; the East African campaign page does not cover it. A bridge, confidence 1.

region.text: Kassala

ledger.note: 18 January 1941: the Italians leave Kassala. The page has the Italians 'on 18 January to retreat hurriedly from Kassala and Tessenei'; the Kassala page: 'In mid-January 1941, the Italians withdrew from the city and a British garrison returned.'

region.text: Cyrenaica, lost to Operation Compass

ledger.note: February 1941: Operation Compass takes Cyrenaica. Tobruk fell on 21 January ('At dawn on 21 January, Australian infantry broke into Tobruk'), the Italians were evacuating Cyrenaica along the Via Balbia from Benghazi in late January, the 10th Army surrendered at Beda Fomm on 5-7 February and on 9 February Churchill ordered the advance to stop at El Agheila.

region.text: Italian Somaliland, without the former British Somaliland

ledger.note: 1941: British forces occupy Italian Somaliland. Infobox 'British occupation: 26 February 1941'; the page gives no date for the capture of Mogadishu.

region.text: Cyrenaica without the besieged Tobruk

ledger.note: March-April 1941: the Axis counter-offensive retakes Cyrenaica. 'The Axis force raided and quickly defeated the British at El Agheila on 24 March', 'Benghazi was captured in April' and 'by 15 April, had pushed the British back to the border at Sollum and besieged Tobruk'. The offensive was German-led; the Italian share is the researcher's reading, confidence 2. Tobruk stayed British.

region.text: British Somaliland

ledger.note: 8 April 1941: British forces recapture British Somaliland. 'British Somaliland was occupied by Italy from 3 August 1940 until 8 April 1941, when British forces recaptured the territory' (lead and infobox 'British recapture: 8 April 1941'); the body says 'In March 1941, after a six-month Italian occupation, British forces recaptured the protectorate during Operation Appearance' and the page does not reconcile the two. british-africa also uses 8 April.

region.text: Eritrea, Asmara and Massawa

ledger.note: 1941: Eritrea falls. Indian troops under William Platt occupied Asmara on 1 April and Massawa on 8 April 1941 (Italian East Africa page).

region.text: Ethiopia except the Gondar pocket

ledger.note: 1941: Addis Ababa falls on 6 April. 'On 6 April 1941, Addis Ababa was seized by the troops of General Alan Cunningham'; the Gondar pocket held out to November.

region.text: the Gondar pocket

ledger.note: 1941: the last Italian stand in East Africa ends at Gondar. 'surrendered after staging a last stand at the Battle of Gondar in November 1941'; infobox 'Allied occupation' 27 November 1941.

region.text: Cyrenaica, recaptured by the British

ledger.note: December 1941: Operation Crusader. 'From 18 November to 30 December'; 'The Axis forces then withdrew to the west of Tobruk to the Gazala Line and then back to El Agheila' and 'Tobruk had been relieved, Cyrenaica recaptured'.

region.text: Cyrenaica west of the Gazala line

ledger.note: January 1942: Operation Theseus. 'Panzerarmee Afrika began Operation Theseus on 21 January'; 'Benghazi fell on 28 January'; 'By 6 February, the British were back to the Gazala line'. The Axis share of Italy is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Tobruk and eastern Cyrenaica

ledger.note: June 1942: Gazala and Tobruk. 'Unternehmen Venezia (the Battle of Gazala) from 26 May to 21 June 1942'; 'Tobruk was captured intact on 22 June'.

region.text: Cyrenaica, where the front swung from December 1940 to November 1942

ledger.note: November 1942: the Eighth Army wins the swings. 'On 4 November, the Eighth Army broke through Axis defences', 'Tobruk was retaken by the Eighth Army on 13 November' and 'Benghazi fell on 20 November'; the Axis retreated through Libya into Tunisia.

region.text: Cyrenaica, lost to the Eighth Army

ledger.note: November 1942: Cyrenaica is lost for good (Tobruk 13 November, Benghazi 20 November).

region.text: the Fezzan, occupied by the Free French

ledger.note: January 1943: the Free French take the Fezzan. 'With British approval, Free French forces moved north from Chad to take control of the territory in January 1943'; they 'occupied the area that was the former Italian Southern Military Territory'. french-africa has the matching occupation from January 1943.

region.text: Tripolitania, the last Italian-held part of Libya

ledger.note: February 1943: Italian rule in Africa ends in Libya. The Western Desert campaign page has the 7th Armoured Division entering Tripoli on 23 January 1943 and dates the campaign 11 June 1940 to 4 February 1943; the last Axis elements reached the Mareth line on 15 February. Tripolitania passes to British military administration; Cyrenaica was lost in November 1942 and the Fezzan to the Free French in January 1943. The Italian Libya infobox gives 13 May 1943 for the end of Italian rule (the Tunisian surrender).

wars.name: First Italo-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian victory: 'Sovereignty of Ethiopia confirmed; border with Italian Eritrea delineated' (treaty of October 1896).
wars.note: 13 January 1895 to 23 October 1896; Adigrat 8 March and Adwa 2 April 1895, annexation of Tigray, the fort at Mekelle surrendered 21 January 1896 and Adwa was fought 1 March 1896.

wars.name: Italo-Turkish War

zones.text: the coastal enclaves of Tripoli, Homs, Benghazi, Derna and Tobruk, the five towns the Italo-Turkish War page names; 20 km radius, the smallest circle the 16 km grid draws (the page gives about 15 km for Tripoli)

wars.outcome: Italian victory: the Treaty of Ouchy (18 October 1912) gave Italy Libya.
wars.note: Declaration 29 September 1911; Tripoli bombarded 3 October; towns taken 3-21 October; sovereignty decree 5 November 1911; the Dodecanese were taken in summer 1912. By the end of 1912 Italy held seven enclaves, five of them named.

wars.name: Pacification of Libya

zones.text: the interior north of the Ghadames-Mizda-Beni Ulid line, the Sirtica and Ghibla, and Cyrenaica

wars.outcome: Italian victory: Tripolitania north of the Ghadames-Mizda-Beni Ulid line (1923-1924), the Sirtica (1924), Ghibla (late 1928), Fezzan (1930) and Kufra (1931) taken; Omar Mukhtar captured September 1931; the campaign declared ended January 1932.

wars.name: Campaign of the Sultanates

zones.text: the Majeerteen (Bari, Nugaal) and Hobyo (Mudug, Galguduud) protectorates

wars.outcome: Italian conquest: Hobyo occupied from 1 October 1925 (dubat columns under Colonel Di Bello) and the Majeerteen not fully taken 'until late 1927'; both sultanates annexed to Italian Somalia.
wars.note: Mussolini gave the green light in 1925 (Italian Somaliland page); the Campaign of the Sultanates page dates the campaign 1925-1927.

wars.name: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: Addis Ababa captured 5 May 1936, Ethiopia annexed 9 May 1936 and merged with Eritrea and Somalia into Italian East Africa on 1 June 1936.
wars.note: The Italian Empire page dates the invasion '1935-36'.

wars.name: East African campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: Kassala and Moyale taken in July 1940 and British Somaliland in August; the Italians left Kassala on 18 January 1941; Italian Somaliland fell on 26 February, Keren on 27 March, Asmara on 1 April, Addis Ababa on 6 April, Massawa on 8 April, British Somaliland was retaken on 8 April and Gondar fell last (November 1941).
wars.note: Italian Empire key dates: 'East Africa Campaign (1940-1941)'.

wars.name: North African campaign (Western Desert campaign)
wars.outcome: Allied victory: the Italian invasion of Egypt (13-18 September 1940) failed at Sidi Barrani (11 December); Operation Compass took Cyrenaica by 9 February 1941, the Axis retook it in April 1941, lost it in Operation Crusader (December 1941), retook it in January and June 1942 and lost it for good in November 1942; Tripoli fell on 23 January 1943 and the Free French took the Fezzan in January 1943.
wars.note: Western Desert campaign infobox: 11 June 1940 to 4 February 1943. The swings are the contest zone over Cyrenaica from December 1940 to November 1942 in the ledger.

certainty.note: Eritrea's frontier is sharp after the Treaty of Addis Ababa (October 1896, 'delineated the borders of Eritrea'); the Somali spheres (Anglo-Italian protocol of 1894) and protectorates are approximate.
Libya's desert frontiers are approximate; Italian control of the interior 'remained limited until the late 1920s'; the Egyptian cession of Jarabub (1925) is a treaty line.
Ethiopia's frontiers were those of the old empire and the colonial lines, all approximate in the desert and highland borderlands.

notes: Italian Africa is a composite of the Italian colonies (Eritrea 1890, Somalia, Libya, Ethiopia 1936); type colony, drawn as a tint of the metropole (kingdom-of-italy). Fix run of 2026-10-24 (after the review of the same day): (1) Libya 1912-1929 is cut from Cliopatria's legal claim (2,946 to 5,091 cells) to what the pages say Italy held: five coastal enclaves in 1912 (the Italo-Turkish War page counts seven and names five towns), Misrata in 1922, Tripolitania north of the Ghadames-Mizda-Beni Ulid line and the Sirtica in 1924, Jarabub in 1925, Ghibla in 1928, the Fezzan in 1930, Kufra in 1931 and Cyrenaica in January 1932; new keyframes 1924, 1925, 1928 and 1931 carry the steps. The enclave circles are 20 km because the 16 km grid draws nothing at 15 km (the page's figure for Tripoli). The interior is contested land in the ledger: against the Senussi order 1912-1917 (Treaty of Acroma), the Tripolitanian rebels 1918-1924 and 1924-1928, and the Senussi in Cyrenaica 1923-1932; the Fezzan is nobody's between its brief Italian suzerainty (August to November 1914) and 1930. (2) The 1920 gain of the western Fezzan is deleted: the Pacification page dates the conquest to 1930, and the 492 cells are an error of Cliopatria's row. (3) Tigray (April 1895 to March 1896) and Kassala (17 July 1894 to the evacuation after Adwa) are gains and losses. (4) The Hobyo occupation is dated 1 October 1925 as in the Hobyo dossier; the Majeerteen contest runs October 1925 to late 1927. (5) 1940-1943 events added from the East African and Western Desert campaign pages. Cliopatria draws Somalia whole from 1895 (all of Jubaland, the Majeerteen and Hobyo protectorates, the Kenya border cells); keyframes 1895-1926 correct this, the ledger gives the dated gains of 1894 (sphere) and 1925 (Jubaland). The south of Libya (Tibesti) is not drawn and the pages do not claim it except the Aouzou strip (1935, unratified). Pages silent on: the Kassala evacuation date (1896 is a bridge), the Moyale return (1941, bridge), the month of the Jubaland transfer, the two unnamed Italian enclaves of 1912, the Italian share of the Axis swings in Cyrenaica (German-led), the month of the Tripoli entry as the end of Italian rule (23 January 1943 against the infobox's 4 February 1943 end of the campaign). Disagreements kept: British Somaliland recaptured 8 April 1941 (lead and infobox) against March 1941 (body); Eritrea 1889 against 1 January 1890; Tobruk 3-21 October against 4 December 1911; Hobyo and Majeerteen protectorates 8 February and 7 April 1889; the Italian Libya infobox end of 13 May 1943 against the Axis exit in February 1943 (this dossier ends in February). The 9 January 1939 incorporation of the coast into metropolitan Italy is a rename event: kingdom-of-italy should not count it as a gain. Counterparts needing a dossier: senussi-order, tripolitanian-republic, anglo-egyptian-sudan; mirrors needed: ethiopian-empire (Tigray 1895 gain and 1896 loss), british-africa (Cyrenaica swings 1941-1942, Kassala and Moyale 1940-1941, Union 1910 against loss 1931, Jubaland 1925, Sarra 1934), mahdist-state (Kassala matches its 1894 loss), french-africa (Fezzan 1943-1 has its occupation; the Rif contest 1925-1926). Gazetteer names wanted: Jubaland (Oltre Giuba), Sarra Triangle, Sidi Barrani (place, Egypt), Ghibla (region). The Aouzou strip (Mussolini-Laval agreement 1935, 'France never ratified it') is deliberately not drawn.
